Corollary
[Cut point in every direction implies compactness] 1. ch13:2.11Suppose $M$ is complete and there exists $p\in M$ which has a cut point for every geodesic starting from $p$. Then $M$ is compact.
Proof

\sketch Since $M=\bigcup \{ \gamma (t);t\leq f(p,\gamma '(0))\} $ over all geodesics $\gamma $ with $\gamma (0)=p$, and $f$ is continuous and (by hypothesis) bounded, $M$ is bounded; the result follows from the Hopf–Rinow Theorem.

□
